:::{#exm-second-order-inconclusive}
#### The condition is sufficient, not necessary

$f(\vx) = x_1^2 + x_2^4$ and $g(\vx) = x_1^2 - x_2^4$
both have gradient $\vzero$ at $\vzero$
and the same Hessian there, $\sbmat{ 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 }$,
since

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{x_2} \paren{\deriv{x_2} (\pm x_2^4)} &= \pm 12 x_2^2 \\
&= 0
\end{aligned}
$$

at $x_2 = 0$.
That Hessian is not positive definite ($\tp{(0, 1)}$ gives $0$),
so @thm-second-order-condition says nothing about either function.
In fact $\vzero$ is a strict local minimizer of $f$,
since $f(\vx) > 0 = f(\vzero)$ for $\vx \ne \vzero$,
but not a local minimizer of $g$, since

$$
\begin{aligned}
g(0, t) &= -t^4 \\
&< 0 \\
&= g(\vzero)
\end{aligned}
$$

for $t \ne 0$.

:::
